fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflectors to help responders locate the access point quickly at night or in reduced visibility.
• Widen or clear vegetation along the sides of the driveway to allow large emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Designate and mark a turnaround area near the residence so that fire and emergency vehicles can reverse direction without getting stuck.
• Keep a flat, firm surface available near the residence for ambulance and fire apparatus staging.
• Trim dense vegetation back from the driveway edge to maintain clear sightlines for drivers of large vehicles navigating the access drive.
• Install a gate lock box or provide a lockbox code to the local fire department if any gate controls access along the driveway.
• Mark any soft ground, ditches, or low shoulders along the driveway edge that could cause a heavy vehicle to become stuck.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or debris so responding units can reach the residence without delay.
• Post a clearly visible address sign at the residence itself, not only at the road, so responders can confirm they have reached the correct structure.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Vegetation Near Structure; Long Driveway; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Woody Debris; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Thin trees closest to the structure to create more open space between the canopy and the roofline.
• Cut and remove grass around the base of the house before it dries out seasonally.
• Clear woody debris such as fallen branches, dead wood, and brush piles from around the structure.
• Remove shrubs growing beneath trees near the house to break up the connection between ground-level plants and tree branches.
• Thin scattered shrubs along the length of the driveway to keep the travel path clear and visible.
• Trim any tree branches overhanging the driveway to allow emergency vehicle clearance.
• Keep the driveway surface free of fallen branches and debris that could block vehicle access.
• Separate shrub clusters near the house so there are open gaps between individual plants.
• Move any stored wood piles, yard debris, or flammable materials away from the exterior walls of the house.
• Remove dead plant material from around any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Cut grass and low vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain clear sightlines and movement along the single access route.
